LAW INVOLVED IN THE PRESENT CASE 18. Section 386 of the IPC provides for the offence of extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt:-
Whoever commits extortion by putting any person in fear of death or of grievous hurt o that person or to any other, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

6 19.

Section 507 of the IPC provides for the offence Criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication: -
Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation by an anonymous communication, or having taken precaution to conceal the name or abode of the person from whom the threat comes, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, in addition to the punishment provided for the offence by the last preceding section.

20. Section 120-B of the IPC provides for the punishment of criminal State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 14 of 20 conspiracy:-
(1) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, 2[imprisonment for life] or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence.
(2) Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both.
21.

At the outset, it is apposite to mention that prosecution has examined two public witnesses i.e PW-2 namely Anurag Puri and PW-8 namely Ashok Puri who is the complainant in the present matter for the purpose of proving its case against accused persons.
Perusal of the testimony of PW-2 reveals that he has received a call regarding the extortion and he has informed his father i.e PW-6 regarding the same.
The star witness of the prosecution is PW-6, however, perusal of his testimony would reveal that he has made several material improvements and contradictions in his testimony before the Court.

Firstly, in the complaint given to the police officials, he has mentioned that he has received ransom call wherein the caller was asking for 1.5 crore whereas in his deposition he has stated that he has received ransom call of Rs. 1.5 lakhs.

Ld. Counsel for accused him confronted PW-6 regarding the same and PW-6 stated State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 15 of 20 that since the ransom calls continue the amount was increased to Rs. 1.5 crore.

sentences.text: It is relevant to that PW-2 has not stated the said fact in his deposition.

During the cross examination,
PW-6 has literally denied all the facts which were stated by other prosecution witnesses.

PW-6 has stated in the cross examination that he does not remember as to who he had informed regarding the extortion call, he does not remember whether the bundles of notes were prepared with Rs. 100 on each side, he does not remember what documents were seized by the police officials, he does not remember that bag carrying the bundles was seized by the police or not and he does not remember whether the disclosure statements of accused persons were recorded or not at the spot.

The perusal of testimony of PW-6 who is the complainant and the star witness of the prosecution reveals that same is inconsistent and suffering from numerous contradictions and does not inspire the confidence of the Court.

It is pertinent to mention that prosecution has heavily relied upon on a hand written note which was seized from accused Mohit wherein certain facts regarding extortion is mentioned.
The IO of the case obtained the handwriting of accused and forwarded the same to FSL and as per FSL result Ex.PW8/G, handwriting of accused matched with the handwriting mentioned on said written.
The mode and way the said written note was seized raises a doubt regarding its genuiness.

It is highly unlikely that an accused person who went to State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 16 of 20 the spot to pick the extortion money will carry the handwritten note in his own hand writing in his pocket.

Even for the argument's sake, it is admitted the said note is written by the accused Mohit and duly seized by the police officials, however, the same will not prove the case of the prosecution when the complainant himself has deposed several contradictory statements in his deposition.
It is also pertinent to mention that expert's evidence is merely an opinion it is not a conclusive proof.
Evidence of handwriting expert needs corroboration from direct or circumstantial evidence.
In Magan Bihari Lal vs State of Punjab AIR 1977 SC 1091, the Supreme Court has held that conviction solely on expert opinion without substantial corroboration is unsafe.

entities.text: Magan Bihari Lal vs State of Punjab AIR 1977 SC 1091
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, when the contents of the complainant are not proved by the prosecution then it will not be safe to accept the version of the prosecution only on the basis of the expert opinion.
23. It is also apposite to mention that IO has not made any investigation regarding the phone numbers from which the said extortion calls are made and, in whose name, the said number belong.
Ideally the IO should have done some investigation to connect the accused persons with the phone numbers which was used for the purpose of making extortion calls to the complainant.

24. It is well settled principle of law that to prove the charge of conspiracy, within the ambit of Section 120-B, it is necessary to establish that there was an State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 17 of 20 agreement between the parties for doing an unlawful act.

At the same time, it is to be noted that it is difficult to establish conspiracy by direct evidence at all, but at the same time, in absence of any evidence to show meeting of minds between the conspirators for the intended object of committing an illegal act, it is not safe to hold a person guilty for offences under Section 120-B of IPC.
A few bits here and a few bits there on which prosecution relies, cannot be held to be adequate for connecting the accused with the commission of crime of criminal conspiracy.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Parveen Vs. State of Haryana Criminal Appeal no. 1571 of 2021 has observed that "it is not safe to hold a person guilty for offences under Section 120B I.P.C.
in absence of any evidence to show a meeting of minds between the conspirators for the intended object of committing an illegal act".

The prosecution has failed to prove the charge of criminal conspiracy against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
25. No doubt wrong acquittals are undesirable and shake the confidence of the people in judicial system, much worse, however, is the wrongful conviction of the innocent man.

In the present case it is pellucid,
that the case of the prosecution suffers from several glaring loopholes as there are numerous inconsistencies in the testimony of the witnesses is found.
27. Therefore, in view of the above said discussion it is pellucid, that the case of the prosecution suffers from several glaring loopholes and there are numerous inconsistencies in the testimonies.
Hence, this court is of the considered opinion, that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.

State vs Parghuman Chauhan on 19 September, 2023

 Judgment

Name of the complainant : Sh. Ashok Puri Name of accused and address : 1. Narender Pal Sharma s/o Sh. Ram Ashre Lal 2. Praghuman Chauhan @ Pintoo Thakur s/o Sh. Ravinder 3. Mohit @ Kalaa s/o Sh. Anil Kumar 4. Subhash (since expired)

Offence complained of or proved : U/s 386/507/120B/34 IPC Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final order : Acquittal Date of judgment : 19.09.2023 BRIEF STATEMENT OF FACTS FOR THE DECISION:-
1. This is the prosecution of the accused namely Parghuman Chauhan @ State V.
Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 1 of 20 Pintoo Thakur,
Bittoo, Mohit @ Kala, Subhash and Narender Pal Sharma upon a charge sheet filed by the police official of police station SP Badli under section 386/507/120-B IPC.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The allegation against the accused persons are that they all in furtherance of their common intention and criminal conspiracy between 21.08.2003 to 26.08.2003 criminally intimidated the complainant Ashok Puri and his son Anurag Puri by an anonymous communication having taken precaution to conceal their identity and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s 507/120-B/34 IPC.
Further, on 26.08.2003, at about 10.15 p.m., near MN Convent Public School, they all in furtherance of their common intention and criminal conspiracy committed the extortion of Rs.2 Lakhs from the complainant by putting him and his son Anurag to fear of death and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 386/120-B/34 IPC.

Thereafter the case property i. e. red cloth, torch, hand written paper and bag were seized by preparing separate seizure.
Thereafter, all the accused persons were arrested.
Thereafter, all the accused persons along with case property were taken to PS State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 8 of 20 SP Badli where his statement was recorded.
He was duly cross examined by Ld.
He further deposed State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 9 of 20 that accused person namely Parghuman Chauhan used to visit their factory for some work/employment.
No certificate U/s 65 of Indian Evidence Act of the then Nodal Officer was on file because in the year 2003, it was not mandatory to issue such a certificate along with the CDR.
He identified the case property as well as the accused during his examination before the court.
He identified the accusd persons during his examination before the court.
All incriminating material brought on record were put to the accused persons, to which they denied the allegations made against them and claimed themselves to be innocent and pleaded that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
Accused persons did not opt to lead any evidence in their defence and the same was closed.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
On the other hand, learned defence counsel contended that State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 13 of 20 the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable shadow of doubt.
Accordingly, he prayed for the acquittal of the accused persons.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The perusal of testimony of PW-6 who is the complainant and the star witness of the prosecution reveals that same is inconsistent and suffering from numerous contradictions and does not inspire the confidence of the Court.
The IO of the case obtained the handwriting of accused and forwarded the same to FSL and as per FSL result Ex.PW8/G, handwriting of accused matched with the handwriting mentioned on said written.
The mode and way the said written note was seized raises a doubt regarding its genuiness.
It is highly unlikely that an accused person who went to State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 16 of 20 the spot to pick the extortion money will carry the handwritten note in his own hand writing in his pocket.
It is also pertinent to mention that expert's evidence is merely an opinion it is not a conclusive proof.
Evidence of handwriting expert needs corroboration from direct or circumstantial evidence.
In Magan Bihari Lal vs State of Punjab AIR 1977 SC 1091, the Supreme Court has held that conviction solely on expert opinion without substantial corroboration is unsafe.
Hence, when the contents of the complainant are not proved by the prosecution then it will not be safe to accept the version of the prosecution only on the basis of the expert opinion.
Ideally the IO should have done some investigation to connect the accused persons with the phone numbers which was used for the purpose of making extortion calls to the complainant.
24. It is well settled principle of law that to prove the charge of conspiracy, within the ambit of Section 120-B, it is necessary to establish that there was an State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No. 17 of 20 agreement between the parties for doing an unlawful act.
At the same time, it is to be noted that it is difficult to establish conspiracy by direct evidence at all, but at the same time, in absence of any evidence to show meeting of minds between the conspirators for the intended object of committing an illegal act, it is not safe to hold a person guilty for offences under Section 120-B of IPC.
A few bits here and a few bits there on which prosecution relies, cannot be held to be adequate for connecting the accused with the commission of crime of criminal conspiracy.
The prosecution has failed to prove the charge of criminal conspiracy against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
25. No doubt wrong acquittals are undesirable and shake the confidence of the people in judicial system, much worse, however, is the wrongful conviction of the innocent man.
The consequences of conviction of innocent men are far State V. Parghuman Chauhan & Ors FIR No. 420/2003 Page No.
18 of 20 more serious and its reverberation would be felt by an innocent all his life in a civilized society, therefore, it is the duty of the court to avoid any wrongful conviction and to grant benefit of State vs Parghuman Chauhan on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197972227/
8 doubt where ever the need arises.
If two views are possible, one favouring the accused and the other against him, the benefit of doubt must be given to the accused and in the instant case, prosecution has failed to prove its case against accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.
26. At this stage, court further deems it fit to state, that it is a settled principle of criminal jurisprudence, that culpability cannot be established on surmises and conjectures but it should rest on cogent, reliable and clinching evidence, dispelling every doubt and bulwarking the fact that in all possibility, the offence must have been committed by the accused.
In the present case it is pellucid,
that the case of the prosecution suffers from several glaring loopholes as there are numerous inconsistencies in the testimony of the witnesses is found.
27. Therefore, in view of the above said discussion it is pellucid, that the case of the prosecution suffers from several glaring loopholes and there are numerous inconsistencies in the testimonies.
Hence, this court is of the considered opinion, that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt.

420/2003 Page No. 19 of 20 Thakur s/o Sh. Ravinder and Mohit @ Kalaa stands acquitted in the present case.
